evidence.claim: Frequent monetary-policy changes and rate cuts since the previous September sent the lira to historic lows, pushed inflation to record highs, and eroded real incomes for poorer households.
evidence.title: Global and Domestic Challenges Weigh on Outlook for Turkish Economy in 2022
evidence.excerpt: Frequent monetary-policy changes and rate cuts since the previous September sent the lira to historic lows, pushed inflation to record highs, and eroded real incomes for poorer households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank country team commentary with explicit 2022 Turkey macro findings and household-impact discussion.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 conditions and the policy path entering 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdoğan-era monetary direction because the report ties the instability to repeated rate cuts and the broader policy setting.
contrary_evidence: Exports boomed in 2021 and growth had been strong before the 2022 slowdown.

evidence.claim: IMF staff said late-2021 rate cuts added vulnerabilities and recommended early policy-rate hikes, stronger central-bank independence, tight fiscal policy, and targeted assistance to vulnerable households.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to Türkiye
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff said late-2021 rate cuts added vulnerabilities and recommended early policy-rate hikes, stronger central-bank independence, tight fiscal policy, and targeted assistance to vulnerable households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF end-of-mission statement is a primary institutional assessment of the 2022 policy mix and its recommended correction.
evidence.period_fit: Directly addresses the 2022 consultation and immediate policy choices affecting 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan because the statement ties the policy path to the government/central bank direction under his authority.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also noted a dynamic private sector and strong rebound from the pandemic.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Türkiye's new policy model relied on low interest rates and directed lending; successive rate cuts triggered a lira run, FX intervention and an FX-protected deposit scheme, while inflation reached 85 percent and quasi-fiscal risks rose.
evidence.title: Republic of Türkiye: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Türkiye's new policy model relied on low interest rates and directed lending; successive rate cuts triggered a lira run, FX intervention and an FX-protected deposit scheme, while inflation reached 85 percent and quasi-fiscal risks rose.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed IMF staff report with explicit diagnosis, 2022 inflation peak, and policy-mechanism description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's chosen macro model and its implementation through the executive/CBRT chain.
contrary_evidence: Türkiye's public debt burden remained low compared to peers.

evidence.claim: The OECD projected 5.3% GDP growth in 2022 but warned that inflation would remain above 40%, household purchasing power would be dented, external financing needs were large, and reserve buffers were low.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 2
evidence.excerpt: The OECD projected 5.3% GDP growth in 2022 but warned that inflation would remain above 40%, household purchasing power would be dented, external financing needs were large, and reserve buffers were low.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD surveillance publication gives contemporaneous macro assessment and a clear household-effect statement.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 conditions and the near-term 2023-24 trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: growth is not purely ruler-driven, but the inflation, financing, and policy context are policy-sensitive under Erdoğan.
contrary_evidence: Growth still remained positive in 2022 and exports continued to support activity.

evidence.claim: The OECD said the CBRT had cut its base rate by 10 points since September 2021 while inflation accelerated and the current account deficit widened, and it described the central-bank policy as accommodative.
evidence.title: Key policy insights: OECD Economic Surveys: Türkiye 2023
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said the CBRT had cut its base rate by 10 points since September 2021 while inflation accelerated and the current account deficit widened, and it described the central-bank policy as accommodative.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD survey text is explicit about the policy direction and its macro effects, though it is analytical rather than audit-based.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the policy trajectory that defined 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan because the rate-cut path was the core policy line he publicly backed and politically controlled.
contrary_evidence: The authorities also tightened macroprudential and collateral requirements.

evidence.claim: The OECD said inflation was especially harmful to vulnerable groups, households in the lowest decile spent nearly 70% of their budget on food and housing, and the government doubled energy assistance to 4 million households while cutting electricity tariffs for low-consumption households.
evidence.title: Key policy insights: OECD Economic Surveys: Türkiye 2023
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said inflation was especially harmful to vulnerable groups, households in the lowest decile spent nearly 70% of their budget on food and housing, and the government doubled energy assistance to 4 million households while cutting electricity tariffs for low-consumption households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD combines distributional analysis with specific 2022 support measures and quantified household exposure.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 distributional policy and effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: the support measures were government policy under Erdoğan, while the household exposure reflects inherited distribution and inflation structure.
contrary_evidence: The same report says the support should be temporary and targeted to limit fiscal costs and preserve price signals.

evidence.claim: Turkey's business environment was undermined by rigid product and labour regulations, an intricate support and taxation system, and slow, heavily backlogged courts that made legal action difficult for companies.
evidence.title: Turkey: Economy Profile: SME Policy Index: Western Balkans and Turkey 2022
evidence.excerpt: Turkey's business environment was undermined by rigid product and labour regulations, an intricate support and taxation system, and slow, heavily backlogged courts that made legal action difficult for companies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD policy assessment with detailed business-environment diagnosis and explicit 2022 country scope.
evidence.period_fit: Current in 2022 and directly relevant to the ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: Erdoğan had broad authority over the policy environment, though some constraints were structural and inherited.
contrary_evidence: The same OECD chapter notes some progress and that SMEs still account for most employment.

evidence.claim: The OECD said only Turkey applied domestic preferences in public procurement, including price advantages for domestic suppliers and domestic-content preferences, which undercut equal treatment in procurement markets.
evidence.title: Public procurement (Dimension 5b) in the Western Balkans and Turkey: SME Policy Index: Western Balkans and Turkey 2022
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said only Turkey applied domestic preferences in public procurement, including price advantages for domestic suppliers and domestic-content preferences, which undercut equal treatment in procurement markets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: OECD procurement assessment gives a direct, explicit description of discriminatory procurement preferences.
evidence.period_fit: The legal and policy framework described was in force in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: procurement rules are state policy under Erdoğan, though they also reflect long-running institutional design.
contrary_evidence: The chapter also notes e-procurement and information access for contracting authorities and firms.

evidence.claim: Freedom House reported that Erdoğan had abruptly fired and replaced the central bank head three times between 2019 and 2021, and that his most recent appointee was a former AKP lawmaker.
evidence.title: Turkey: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House reported that Erdoğan had abruptly fired and replaced the central bank head three times between 2019 and 2021, and that his most recent appointee was a former AKP lawmaker.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Freedom House is a standard secondary monitor with a specific, attributable statement about appointments and independence erosion.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline and continuing governance context entering 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan's appointment power and intervention in the monetary team.
contrary_evidence: The report frames this as part of a 2019-2021 pattern rather than a new 2022 appointment cycle.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said corruption remained a major problem, with holding companies capturing a vast portion of public tenders, including Erdoğan mega-projects, and controlling most of Turkey's media networks; it also noted the seizure of hundreds of businesses and NGOs since 2016.
evidence.title: Turkey: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said corruption remained a major problem, with holding companies capturing a vast portion of public tenders, including Erdoğan mega-projects, and controlling most of Turkey's media networks; it also noted the seizure of hundreds of businesses and NGOs since 2016.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific corruption and capture findings from a major rights monitor, directly tied to public-tender allocation and state seizure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: these are governance outcomes under Erdoğan's long tenure and control of the executive state.
contrary_evidence: The passage describes a long-running pattern since 2016, so not every instance is uniquely 2022-specific.

evidence.claim: Transparency International said powerful patronage networks had infiltrated Turkish state institutions, weakening independent oversight and prosecution and allowing corrupt officials and organized criminals to act with impunity.
evidence.title: Turkey
evidence.excerpt: Transparency International said powerful patronage networks had infiltrated Turkish state institutions, weakening independent oversight and prosecution and allowing corrupt officials and organized criminals to act with impunity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The knowledge hub is a credible cross-country corruption resource, but the page is high-level and not a year-specific audit.
evidence.period_fit: General context still relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable only in part: it describes systemic patronage under the governing order rather than a single 2022 decision.
contrary_evidence: The page is regional and broad rather than a Turkey-only audit with dated 2022 incidents.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan reiterated his unorthodox policy, saying interest rates would be lowered and inflation would fall, while Reuters described the economy as already in a currency crisis fueled by previous rate cuts.
evidence.title: Erdogan says interest rates will be lowered and inflation will fall too
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan reiterated his unorthodox policy, saying interest rates would be lowered and inflation would fall, while Reuters described the economy as already in a currency crisis fueled by previous rate cuts.
evidence.source_locator: lead and body excerpt in search result / article intro
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire text is reliable on the quoted statement and contemporaneous market reaction, though the host page is a secondary mirror.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Erdoğan's public economic line.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because the statement is Erdoğan's own public policy stance.
contrary_evidence: This was rhetoric plus a forecast, not proof of implementation quality by itself.

evidence.claim: Turkey's central bank cut the policy rate to 13 percent despite inflation near 80 percent, saying it needed to keep driving growth, and Reuters noted the move followed Erdogan's unorthodox policy path.
evidence.title: Turkey's cenbank shocks with 100 basis point rate cut despite soaring inflation
evidence.excerpt: Turkey's central bank cut the policy rate to 13 percent despite inflation near 80 percent, saying it needed to keep driving growth, and Reuters noted the move followed Erdogan's unorthodox policy path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete policy action with immediate macro context and explicit attribution to the policy line Erdogan advocated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Erdoğan-backed monetary strategy, even though the formal action was taken by the CBRT.
contrary_evidence: The bank said it wanted to keep driving economic growth, so the move had a stated growth rationale even if the inflation tradeoff was severe.

evidence.claim: Reuters said Nureddin Nebati was picked by President Erdoğan to oversee and articulate an unorthodox policy of lowering interest rates amid spiraling inflation and a tumbling currency, and even some pro-government sources wanted a more market-friendly figure.
evidence.title: Turkey's new finance minister in the eye of a storm
evidence.excerpt: Reuters said Nureddin Nebati was picked by President Erdoğan to oversee and articulate an unorthodox policy of lowering interest rates amid spiraling inflation and a tumbling currency, and even some pro-government sources wanted a more market-friendly figure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters text is credible for the appointment and the contemporaneous market concern, though the host page is a mirror.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 ruler-period and about the top economic appointment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because the appointment was Erdoğan's choice and the article discusses his chosen policy line.
contrary_evidence: Nebati was expected to articulate rather than redesign the policy, so the source is stronger on appointment quality than on delivered outcomes.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Turkey had rapidly increased renewable-energy production and expanded waste-treatment infrastructure, and that leadership announcements pointed to ambitious climate and resilience plans supported by the financial sector.
evidence.title: Financing the Next Generation of Green Growth and Prosperity in Turkey
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Turkey had rapidly increased renewable-energy production and expanded waste-treatment infrastructure, and that leadership announcements pointed to ambitious climate and resilience plans supported by the financial sector.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank analysis is credible on sectoral investment and green-growth foundations, but it is partly prospective and not a direct implementation audit.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and discussing the policy direction active in that period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: the report cites leadership announcements and policy framing, but much of the content is sectoral and prospective rather than a ruler-order outcome.
contrary_evidence: The report also says green finance is still evolving and short-term funding structures and other barriers limit growth.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 nuclear-specific conduct is sparse; most positive evidence is alliance or humanitarian diplomacy rather than nuclear command, doctrine, or safety reform.
The package shows limited exposure and inherited NATO structure, but not a strong ruler-attributed improvement or deterioration in nuclear posture.

The package is strong on mediation and selective coercion, but weaker on independent verification of the civilian-harm allegations and on Erdoğan's own weighing of peaceful alternatives for the Syria/Iraq operations.
Several items are civic-space or press-repression evidence rather than direct physical-integrity harm, so the chapter partly relies on fear-climate inference.
Attribution for some harms is institutional rather than command-specific, especially for local policing and court actions.
There was no true 2022 succession or term-limit stress test, so the chapter relies on institutional erosion and media/election-law evidence instead of a direct transfer-of-power event.
Outcomes are heavily confounded by inflation shocks, external demand, the post-pandemic rebound, and CBRT formal independence, so causal credit remains partial.
Project-level delivery and regional/household distribution evidence are thinner than macro indicators.
The strongest welfare evidence is on health coverage and refugee cash transfers; housing, sanitation, and school-quality evidence is thinner.
Several positive items are donor-UNICEF/WHO partnerships, so Erdoğan attribution is meaningful but not exclusive.
There is no direct 2022 audited asset, gift, or procurement record for Erdoğan personally.
The strongest negative items are media-control and family-network allegations, not direct first-person dishonesty or self-dealing proof.
Project-level completion evidence is thin; the package shows allocation, program design, and some outcomes, but not audited delivery for specific 2022 initiatives.
Outcome attribution is still confounded by shocks and by private-sector behavior, especially on growth, exports, and labor-market statistics.
